text.p: $PRODUCT relies on a trace recorder library included in the target system. We support several third party tracing libraries and also provide our very own solution, TraceRecorder, that is used in several of the provided RTOS integrations.
To learn how to apply $PNAME on your particular target system, please refer to the corresponding section in this chapter.

$PRODUCT uses Percepio TraceRecorder to record traces on the target system. This is an event tracing library designed for embedded software systems and the Percepio trace visualization tools. The TraceRecorder library is implemented in C (C99) and provided with full source code under the Apache 2.0 license.

To add TraceRecorder to your target system build, follow the Getting Started guide corresponding to your RTOS. Make sure to follow the steps for "snapshot tracing" using the "RingBuffer" stream port module. Trace streaming is only supported with Percepio Profile or Percepio Tracealyzer. No manual instrumentation is required to record kernel events.

$PRODUCT uses Percepio TraceRecorder to record traces on the target system. This is an event tracing library designed for embedded software systems and the Percepio trace visualization tools. The TraceRecorder library is implemented in C (C99) and provided with full source code under the Apache 2.0 license.
To add TraceRecorder to your target system build, follow the Getting Started guide corresponding to your RTOS. No manual instrumentation is required to record kernel events.

ul.li: Task scheduling and RTOS API calls are traced automatically, using existing kernel trace hooks.
Interrupt service routines (ISRs) can be traced by adding calls to xTraceISRBegin() and xTraceISREnd() in your interrupt handlers. See the TraceRecorder ISR functions in trcISR.h for details.

You may log custom User Events using the following logging functions in the trcPrint API.
xTracePrint() - Basic string logging
xTracePrintF() - Logging with variable number of arguments (e.g. "%d")
xTracePrintF0() .. xTracePrintF4() - Logging with fixed number of arguments (faster).
xTraceConsoleChannelPrintF - Drop-in replacement for printf, intended for redirecting existing logging.
This is useful as debug messages, to see more information about what your code is doing, and has minimal overhead - can be 100x faster than a traditional printf call over a UART.

text.p: The API functions in trcPrint.h and trcISR.h are accessed by including the main header file, trcRecorder.h. Note that other tracing functions in TraceRecorder, such as interval-, state machine- and runnable tracing, and the "Compact Log" functions in trcPrint.h (e.g. xTracePrintCompactF1), are only supported using Percepio Tracealyzer.

ul.li: Each traced event typically adds a some microseconds of execution time, depending on processor speed and compiler optimizations.

The ISR tracing support is mainly intended for debugging purposes. It is recommended to only use ISR tracing for specific ISRs that are important for the issue at hand. This is not intended for system handlers like the tick interrupt. Tracing all ISRs, or very frequent ISRs, may cause significant overhead.

If using TraceRecorder for profiling, note that the tracing overhead will inflate the reported metrics by some microseconds, which can be significant for very short execution times in the microsecond range.
If ISR tracing is not used, the CPU time spent in ISRs will instead be attributed to the currently running task.
